newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita, US jobs data boost Helsinki to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Merita, US jobs data boost Helsinki to new highs.

text.p: Finnish shares hit a new life-high in lively late afternoon dealings as the U.S. unemployment rate rose despite an increase in jobs, soothing fears of a coming rate hike, brokers said.

The general HEX index rose 1.1 percent, closing at 2,806.08 points, over 21 points above its previous record close set on January 23. Active late dealings lifted overall volume to a healthy 722 million with 39.6 percent in telecoms major Nokia.
"We got bullish as U.S. non-farm payrolls data indicated that benign inflation continues there," one broker said.

Finland's largest banking group Merita rose 0.60 markka or over 3.5 percent to 17.40 on speculation of a coming merger in the financial sector and on dividend hopes ahead of its 1996 report due on Wednesday.
"Earnings reports will set tone next week, particularly Nokia's report on Wednesday," said another.

Nokia's 1996 pretax profit was seen at 3.85 billion markka, down from the 1995 record of 4.93 billion, but a continued recovery with the fourth quarter at 1.62 billion compared to 1.1 billion in the third. Nokia rose 2.20 markka to 323.20 after it said it sold its tuner operation.
Shipping firm Finnlines eased on profit taking after an in-line 1996 report and flat prospects, down 3.50 markka at 126.50.
Lift-maker Kone fell despite higher-than-expected 1996 profits on its cautious outlook, down 5.00 markka at 555.00 in moderate trade.
